prompt: Write a miniature pom.xml reader that extracts <properties>, then lists every dependency with its ${...} version resolved. Complete MiniPomAnalyzer, then run the tests.
explanation: The job splits into two reusable helpers: section cuts out the text inside one element, and tagValue reads a single child value -- so slicing one <dependency> block and then querying it keeps each dependency's fields from bleeding into the next. properties cannot use tagValue because the child names are not known in advance, so it scans for '<' ... '>' to learn each name and then looks for the matching closing tag. LinkedHashMap preserves document order, and resolving ${name} only when the key exists is what leaves an unknown property visible in the report instead of silently blanking it.
hints: Write two small private helpers first: one that returns the text INSIDE <tag>...</tag>, and one that returns a single child value from a block.
For dependencies, find each "<dependency>" and its "</dependency>", substring that block out, and read groupId/artifactId/version/scope from the block only -- not from the whole pom.
properties has to discover names it does not know: find the next '<', read up to '>' to get the name, skip it when it starts with '/', then look for "</name>".
